summary: The tellings of the Old Faith read against the Gaelic tales. On the map one note changes: the sacred wood of Macha's order (marker 24) is the wood of Dubh Sainglenn, the black horse, whose yoke-fellow is Liath Macha, the Grey of Macha; the two drew one chariot and were foaled on one night, two horses and not one beast. The faiths list and its deities (an Dagda, na Sìthichean, Crìosd) and marker 23 (Flidais's grove and her white stag) agree with the tales and are unchanged.

skip.why: replaced by the note below, which keeps Dubh Sainglenn and Liath Macha as two horses of one chariot

map_edits.value: A forest sacred to Macha, where Òrd Mhacha keeps the wood of Dubh Sainglenn, the black horse, yoke-fellow of Liath Macha, the Grey of Macha: the two horses of one chariot, foaled on one night.
map_edits.why: Liath Macha and Dubh Sainglenn are Cù Chulainn's two chariot horses, foaled on the night he was born; the order keeps the pair as its sign
